new_entities.name: Continuous glucose monitoring in noninsulin-treated type 2 diabetes
aliases: CGM in type 2 diabetes not using insulin
continuous glucose monitoring for noninsulin-treated T2D
new_entities.description: Use of continuous glucose monitoring in adults with type 2 diabetes who are not treated with insulin.

new_entities.name: Hemoglobin A1c
new_entities.description: Glycated hemoglobin as a marker of average glycemic control over the preceding two to three months.

edges.effect_quant: Recent randomized evidence in noninsulin-treated type 2 diabetes points toward modest HbA1c improvement with CGM, typically around a 0.3% to 0.4% advantage over standard monitoring or education-based comparators, but the magnitude is not large and depends on how much education, behavior change support, and treatment intensification accompany device use.
edges.population: adults with type 2 diabetes who are not using insulin therapy
edges.mechanism: CGM can make postprandial excursions and day-to-day glycemic patterns visible, allowing behavior change, improved self-management, and more targeted treatment adjustments that may reduce HbA1c.
edges.summary: This is best framed as a mixed but favorable signal. The direction is usually beneficial, but the effect size is modest and some of the gain may come from the education and engagement that often travel with CGM rather than from the sensor alone.
edges.caveats: Trial durations are relatively short, some interventions bundle CGM with educator support, and the incremental benefit may be smaller in patients with lower baseline HbA1c or limited willingness to act on the data.
